name: Weak metrics: grab-bag of vanity metrics for an audio huddle feature

scenario.title: Define success metrics for lightweight audio huddles
scenario.problemStatement: A workplace chat tool added 'huddles': one-click audio calls inside a channel. How do you measure the feature's success?

clarificationQuestions: What problem does huddles solve: replacing scheduled meetings, faster unblocking?
Who is the customer: end user vs paying admin; is it on paid tiers?
Stage of feature and expected usage pattern
How does it relate to integrations with other video tools?
coreHypothesesOrSegments: User value: quick resolution of conversations
Team/workspace value: fewer scheduled meetings, faster collaboration
Business value: paid seat retention and upgrade
analyticalPath: North Star such as weekly workspaces with repeated huddle use
Inputs: start rate, join rate, repeat usage
Guardrails: notification mutes, message activity, call quality
benchmarkOutline.synthesisModel: North Star + inputs + guardrails with a decision plan.

scratchpadNotes: huddles. downloads, DAU, revenue, NPS, minutes

messages.text: We added huddles to our workplace chat app, one-click audio calls inside a channel. How would you measure success?
I would look at downloads of the app, DAU, MAU, revenue, NPS, total huddle minutes, and number of huddles started. If those go up, the feature is successful.
Downloads of the app? How would huddles show up there?
Well if huddles is popular, more people will download the app to use it. So downloads should go up. And DAU too.
Which one of these would you pick as the main metric?
Total huddle minutes, because more minutes means people like it more. If people are talking a lot it means huddles are working.
Could more minutes ever be a bad thing?
I don't think so. More usage is always good for the product. Maybe if the audio quality is bad, but then minutes would go down anyway.
Okay. Who is this feature for, and how does it make money?
It's for everyone who uses the app. It makes money because companies pay for the app, so if people use it more, revenue goes up.
How would you summarize your recommendation?
Track all of them on a dashboard: downloads, DAU, MAU, revenue, NPS, huddle minutes, huddles started, and maybe number of channels. If they go up after launch, huddles is a success.
